item.title: Jaguars offense gets an F for a sloppy, clunky effort in loss to Giants
item.description: Grading the Jacksonville Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the New York Giants on Nov. 22 in East Rutherford, N.J. The Jaguars (7-3) will return home after three road games in a row to host the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 29 at EverBank Stadium. Offense: F Yuck. Start with nine offensive penalties, including four false starts by four players. There was an illegal formation, an illegal shift, a delay penalty and quarterback Trevor Lawrence came through with an oldie, but never a goodie, throwing a pass beyond the line of scrimmage ... and it wasn't close. Lawrence had three interceptions if you count the one on a two-point conversion attempt (it's not) and many of his incompletions were high. He was sacked three times and was hit eight other times. The running game struggled because the Giants' defensive line overpowered the Jags offensive line. It was a basic as football gets. The Jaguars scored only one touchdown in six trips to the red zone against a defense that had given up touchdowns on 80 percent of their oppositions' trips inside the 20-yard line. What else? How about 5 of 15 on third down (failing to convert on their first seven when it was third-and-eight or longer) and failing to punch the ball in after two shots with 2 yards to go in the third quarter? It was a mess. Defense: B This was a borderline A until the Giants' last possession, when the Jags absolutely, positively had to get the ball back with 3:40 left in the game and only one time out left. But J.J. McCarthy his Malachi Fields for 19 yards and Cam Skattebo ran for two 5-yard gains to give the Giants a first down at the two-minute warning, enabling the victory formation. Also detracting from the final grade was losing contain on McCarthy, who had a 22-yard scramble on third-and-five and a 13-yard gain on third-and-eight. He had another 29-yard run nullified by a penalty. Other than that, the Jaguars' defense played well enough to give the offense a chance. The Jaguars failed to score after Antonio Harrison's 42-yard fumble return and a missed 32-yard field goal by Dominic Zvada. Josh Hines-Allen had his first solo sack since the opening game of the season but McCarthy got hit only three other times. Skattebo was no factor until the final possession (14 carries, 34 yards, 2.4 yards per attempt) and McCarthy threw some terrible passes, with a final rating of 69.3. Malik Nabers got a TD pass but was otherwise invisible and tight end Isaiah Likely caught only one pass. It was a big one, 35 yards, but went for naught when Zavada hooked his field-goal attempt. Special teams: C For the third game in a row, Cam Little made all four of his field goal attempts, and he's made 18 in a row and 22 of 24 this season. Ameer Abdullah gave the Jaguars great field position with a 47-yard return of the opening kickoff but after getting a first down to the Giants' 14, the offense stalled and Little kicked his first field goal. item.title: SEC Rivalry Week Schedule Sets Up a Dramatic Finish With Plenty at Stake
item.description: Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back Bray Hubbard (18) celebrates his interception as Auburn Tigers take on Alabama Crimson Tide in the Iron Bowl at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Ala. on Saturday, Nov. 29, 2025. Alabama Crimson Tide defeated Auburn Tigers 27-20. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference has saved some of its most anticipated matchups for last. Rivalry Week arrives Friday, Nov. 27, with conference championship implications, postseason positioning and decades of bad blood sharing the spotlight. Georgia has already secured its place in the SEC Championship Game. However, Alabama, Tennessee and Texas still have unfinished business. Meanwhile, several other programs have an opportunity to close their seasons with bragging rights that last considerably longer than one Saturday. Complete SEC Rivalry Week schedule All times Eastern. Date Matchup Time TV Friday, Nov. 27 Mississippi State at Ole Miss Noon ABC Friday, Nov. 27 Florida at Florida State 3:30 p.m. ABC Friday, Nov. 27 Texas at Texas A&M 7:30 p.m. ABC Saturday, Nov. 28 Louisville at Kentucky Noon ESPN2 Saturday, Nov. 28 LSU at Arkansas 12:45 p.m. SEC Network Saturday, Nov. 28 South Carolina at Clemson 3 or 3:30 p.m. ESPN, ESPN2 or ACC Network Saturday, Nov. 28 Georgia Tech at Georgia 3:30 p.m. ABC Saturday, Nov. 28 Oklahoma at Missouri 4:15 p.m. SEC Network Saturday, Nov. 28 Tennessee at Vanderbilt 7 p.m. ESPN Saturday, Nov. 28 Auburn at Alabama 7:30 p.m. ABC South Carolina-Clemson’s exact kickoff time and television assignment remain among the options listed by the conference. Friday could change everything Texas visits Texas A&M on Friday night, giving the Longhorns the first opportunity to influence the SEC Championship Game race. A victory would improve Texas to 7-2 in conference play and place pressure on Alabama and Tennessee entering Saturday. However, a loss would eliminate the Longhorns from contention for the conference title game. Earlier Friday, Ole Miss hosts Mississippi State in the Egg Bowl. Florida also travels to Tallahassee for its annual meeting with Florida State. Saturday brings the biggest decisions Georgia hosts Georgia Tech in Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate, although the Bulldogs have already completed their SEC schedule. Meanwhile, Tennessee visits Vanderbilt before Alabama hosts Auburn in the Iron Bowl. Those two games could determine which team joins Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5. Elsewhere, Oklahoma travels to Missouri, South Carolina visits Clemson and Kentucky hosts Louisville. The regular season has produced plenty of surprises. Nevertheless, Rivalry Week has a way of making everything that happened before it feel like an opening act. For the SEC, the final weekend promises more than bragging rights. It will help determine the conference’s championship matchup and shape its playoff representation. Check out Week 13 College Football scores here: View our latest SEC Country articles here:

item.title: 49ers’ Colton McKivitz suffers horrifying leg injury in Mexico City
item.description: San Francisco 49ers offensive lineman Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury during Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. McKivitz — who had played in 77 straight games entering the game — seemed to snap his lower leg while blocking during a play. San Francisco 49ers offensive lineman Colton McKivitz suffered an injury against the Minnesota Vikings. (@MLFootball) The broadcast showed his left foot seemingly twisted to the side before cutting to a timeout. When they returned, many 49ers players were visibly shaken up and taking a knee. It is way too early to tell exactly what happened to the 30-year-old lineman. But there’s no doubt that this was a very serious injury. HEARTBREAKING FOOTAGE #49ers STANDOUT TACKLE COLTON MCKIVITZ JUST SUFFERED A HORRIFIC INJURY ON THE FIELD. MCKIVITZ IMMEDIATELY WENT DOWN, GRABBING AT HIS INJURY AND SCREAMING IN PAIN. TRENT WILLIAMS HAD AN EMOTIONAL OUTBURST WATCHING THE SCENE UNFOLD. pic.twitter.com/QgkfGnujwe — MLFootball (@MLFootball) November 23, 2026 A close-up of Colton McKivitz’s injury during the San Francisco 49ers-Minnesota Vikings game. (X/@MLFootball). This is a tough loss for the 49ers, who have one of the league’s best offensive lines. But the hope right now is that McKivitz’s injury isn’t as bad as it looked. There is surely more to come on his injury’s severity.

item.title: Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were sent crashing back to earth after losing to the New York Jets, 27-24 , at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. All the high from the Chargers’ win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 10 was erased, and it could be more costly, as Herbert was placed in concussion protocol. He played the entire game without exiting for a sideline evaluation. The Chargers have not specified the exact play on which he got hurt. The 28-year-old quarterback did not face the media , as noted by KTLA’s Hayley Elwood. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol per Chargers PR. He will not be speaking postgame,” wrote Elwood on X. Herbert absorbed significant punishment against the Jets, taking six sacks and eight hits. He suffered a smack to the facemask from David Bailey in the second quarter, which drew a roughing-the-passer call. The two-time Pro Bowler threw 15-of-21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns. He also scored on a short rush to end the first half. The Chargers remained winless at home and fell to 1-9. The Jets, meanwhile, broke their five-game losing streak to the Chargers and improved to 3-8. The much-hyped pairing of Herbert and Mike McDaniel has not worked, and Los Angeles is in danger of missing the playoffs for the second time in four years. If Herbert is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Week 12 against the New England Patriots, DJ Uiagalelei is next in line to start, with Trey Lance out with a groin injury and Jake Browning on the practice squad. item.title: Jalen Smith doing it all as Bulls attempts to right ship
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images Jalen Smith doing it all as Bulls attempts to right ship appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bulls are looking to bounce back. They just went on an eight-game losing streak. Plus, they lost Caleb Wilson to a broken hand for at least six weeks. On Sunday, they welcomed the Denver Nuggets to complete a week in which they played four games. With Nic Claxton out with an illness , Jalen Smith once again filled in at center. And it was a good thing, even though he was listed as probable due to illness himself. He was virtually all over the floor. Smith took good shots, went for rebounds, and showed pure versatility. All of which came together in one sequence in the 2nd quarter. At the 7:53 mark, Tre Jones went for the 3-pointer, but missed. Smith grabbed the rebound and kicked it back out to Jones. Jones pumped-faked it before finding the open Buddy Hield on the wing. Hield penetrated the lane, dished it to Smith, who then slammed it down with authority. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) JALEN SMITH IS DOING IT ALL RIGHT NOW! He has 15 first half points 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/xNYLykk9gF — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 23, 2026 He finished the half with 15 points and went 6-for-7 from the field. In Claxton’s absence, Smith has emerged as a major catalyst at center. Altogether, he is averaging 13.4 points and 7.9 rebounds per game while shooting 52.8% from the field. Additionally, Smith has scored in double figures in 11 games this season. His highest-scoring game came on November 11 against the San Antonio Spurs, when he finished with 23 points. Meanwhile, Smith has bounced back from injury scares , usually stemming from aggressive play. Chicago trailed Denver 72-70 at the half. The Bulls will play the Cleveland Cavaliers at home on Monday at 7:00 pm CST/8:00 pm EST. item.title: 34 Years Later, the Best 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless
item.description: Larson didn’t do deep and inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful . Larson’s work was brilliant, and it sometimes took a few minutes to figure out what the punchline was. Take, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature, for example. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly stuck to his glasses.

item.title: Pierre LeBrun Reveals Stunning Dylan Larkin Trade Secret Kept Quiet for Months
item.description: The Dylan Larkin trade saga finally came to an end Sunday night when the Detroit Red Wings sent their former captain to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal. But according to NHL insider Pierre LeBrun , there was a major secret being kept behind the scenes for months. And it changes the way we look at how this entire situation unfolded. Following the trade, LeBrun revealed that Larkin had actually been willing to accept a move to Montreal for more than two months. However, the Canadiens and Larkin’s representatives reportedly agreed to keep that information quiet. “So, it turns out Dylan Larkin was actually open to a trade to Montreal for more than two months,” LeBrun wrote on X, according to the post provided. “But the Canadiens wanted to keep that quiet because they felt it would add an extra layer of noise that might hamper getting a deal done. And Larkin’s camp agreed.” That’s a fascinating revelation considering the months of speculation surrounding Larkin’s approved trade destinations. Oct 26, 2026; Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; Edmonton Oilers defensemen Ryan Shea (6) looks to clear the puck in front of Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) during the second period at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Michael Hage Was the Key to Getting the Deal Done According to LeBrun, Montreal had been a legitimate possibility much longer than the public realized. However, the Canadiens still had to satisfy Detroit’s asking price, which reportedly included one particularly important asset. Michael Hage. “Montreal agreeing to include Hage was a huge must for the Red Wings,” LeBrun reported. “The deal started to come together and get serious on Friday.” That detail is especially interesting considering Hage had previously emerged as a potential centerpiece in a hypothetical deal between the two organizations. Now, we know just how important the 20-year-old University of Michigan standout was to Detroit’s negotiations. According to the NHL’s official trade announcement , the Red Wings received Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, two conditional first-round picks, a second-round selection, and a fourth-round pick. Montreal received Larkin, along with Detroit’s 2027 third-round and 2028 second-round selections. LeBrun’s Revelation Raises New Questions Perhaps the most interesting aspect of LeBrun’s report is how it contrasts with the information available throughout the trade saga. Earlier this month, reports indicated Larkin’s camp was unwilling to expand his approved list , even as Montreal continued expressing interest. Now, LeBrun’s latest account suggests the Canadiens had privately received Larkin’s blessing long before Sunday’s announcement. That doesn’t necessarily mean the earlier reporting was inaccurate. It does, however, suggest there was considerably more happening behind the scenes than the public knew. For Detroit, the biggest takeaway may be that interim gen

item.title: Dylan Larkin traded to Montreal Canadiens for goalie, package of picks
item.description: The divorce between the Detroit Red Wings and disgruntled former captain Dylan Larkin is finally complete. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff traded Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday, Nov. 22, acquiring forwards Kirby Dach, Michigan Wolverines prospect Michael Hage, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and a second round pick in 2028 and a fourth-round pick in 2028. Larkin is in Year 4 of an eight-year deal carrying an $8.7 million salary cap hit that is highly favorable in a league where the 2026-27 salary cap ceiling is $104 million. Larkin, 30, signed an eight-year, $69.6 million extension with the Wings on March 1, 2023. DYLAN BUCKS: Larkin tops $1 million forfeited while awaiting Red Wings trade Larkin had two goals and four assists in 10 games for the Wings this season, before leaving the team on Oct. 29. The Wings suspended Larkin without pay that same day , costing him $41,237.11 a day. Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, told reporters, "Dylan’s had enough of the situation." Sunday monrig marked more than $1 million of salary forfeited back to the team. Larkin's final goal in a Wings uniform came Oct. 26, tying the game late in the third period at Edmonton in an eventual thrilling shootout win. He didn't play again. LARKIN LATE TYING GOAL 🚨 Red Wings applying massive pressure with the empty net - Seider finds Raymond who gets it to Larkin for the game tying tally. Detroit sends it to overtime. #LGRW pic.twitter.com/yCVN8muhU7 — Ryan Hana (@RyanHanaWWP) October 27, 2026 Larkin was soundly booed by his hometown fans when he was introduced during opening night Oct. 2 at Little Caesars Arena while out with an upper-body injury sustained in the offseason . Larkin was again booed in his season debut Oct. 6 after missing the season's first two games, but turned jeers to cheers after scoring a goal and being named the game's first star. Montreal fans at Bell Centre chanted "We want Larkin!" on Oct. 10, the most notable away crowd reaction to the saga. News broke on June 4 that Larkin, who had a no-trade clause, had requested a trade after 11 seasons with his hometown Wings. Larkin is from nearby Waterford, attended the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor and had been the Wings' captain until he was stripped of the title after the trade request became public. Larkin has gone 10 years without appearing in the NHL playoffs – the Wings own the NHL's longest playoff drought – and his gold-medal success at the 2026 Milano Olympics likely reminded him how fun it is to win important games. He returned to Detroit from that experience, and watched as a Wings team that had been 10 points inside the playoff picture in late January lost its foothold and dropped out of contention, again. Steve Yzerman, removed as GM in July , said shortly after the season he received a phone call from Larkin's agent informing him Larkin wanted to be traded. A week later, a list of teams Larkin would waive his no-trade clause for was provided

item.title: Steelers Star Ejected After Eye-Poke in Loss to Eagles
item.description: Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf (4) shoves Philadelphia Eagles safety Marcus Epps (29) and gets ejected during the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was disqualified in the third quarter of Sunday’s 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles after drawing his second personal foul of the game. The sequence began earlier when Metcalf got into a shoving match with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean and was flagged for unnecessary roughness. Later in the quarter, after an incomplete pass, Metcalf and DeJean tangled again away from the play. Replays showed Metcalf reaching through DeJean’s facemask and appearing to poke him in the eye area. Officials called unsportsmanlike conduct. Because it was Metcalf’s second such penalty, he was automatically ejected under NFL rules. FULL SEQUENCE: Here’s what led to #Steelers WR D.K. Metcalf getting ejected from the game vs the #Eagles for unsportsmanlike conduct. Plus, an extra angle that shows what appears like an eye-poking in Cooper DeJean’s face. Metcalf’s head nod after the ruling looks like he… pic.twitter.com/GJXthKarKx — JosinaAnderson (@JosinaAnderson) November 22, 2026 At the time of the ejection, Metcalf had just one catch for two yards on four targets. He left the field without further comment and exited the locker room before media availability. It marked his third career disqualification since entering the league in 2019. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy called the ejection unacceptable, noting the team needs Metcalf on the field. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers described it as disappointing, saying the club cannot afford two penalties of that kind. The loss dropped Pittsburgh further in the AFC playoff picture on a day when the offense already struggled to generate points. Metcalf’s on-field production has been inconsistent in 2026. He entered the game with modest yardage and touchdown totals for a high-priced receiver acquired via trade and given a large extension. As a repeat offender with prior ejections and a two-game suspension last season for an altercation involving a fan, he faces the possibility of additional league discipline, including a fine or suspension. The Steelers will prepare for their next game without knowing whether their top wideout will be available. The ejection added another costly distraction to an already difficult afternoon in Philadelphia.

item.title: Weekend Warm-up: Did Bayern Munich do the right thing in signing Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies to massive deals?
item.description: (Photo by Marcel Engelbrecht - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is an uncomfortable question hanging over Bayern Munich’s recent contract strategy — did the club make the right investments in Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies, or did it allow the fear of losing two exceptional talents to dictate financial decisions that could eventually become difficult to justify? Both players received lucrative, long-term extensions in February 2025. At the time, Bayern Munich vie wed them as essential building blocks for the future. Musiala was arguably the most exciting young attacking talent in German football, while Davies remained one of Eur ope’s most sought-after left-backs. Losing either player, particularly on a free transfer, would have been a significant sporting and financial setback. At the time that each signed, it was reported that neither had a serious suito r. But there was another consideration that could not be ignored — neither player had an entirely clean injury history. Bayern Munich was committing enormous money to two footballers whose availability had already become a recurring concern. That concern has become considerably harder to dismiss since the contracts were signed. The numbers from Transfermarkt provide some perspective on why Bayern Munich’s decision deserves scrutiny. Its seasonal injury-history summaries include both days unavailable and matches missed, althou gh the records also include some non-injury absences, such as illness, quarantine, and fitness-related issues. A hamstring injury in November 2023, recurring muscle problems, and a torn muscle bundle in April 2025 interrupted his progress. Then came the devastating broken fibula sustained at the Club World Cup in July 2025, which kept him out for 174 days and 31 matches. item.title: Fed-up Cal Bears fans curse out players after Stanford rout in Big Game
item.description: Some Cal football fans have had enough. Following the Golden Bears’ rough 44-28 loss in the “Big Game” to their cross-bay rivals Stanford, falling to 3-8 on the season, fans were caught on video cursing out players as they left the field. It’s never good when opposing fans rush the field in your home stadium. But that’s not an excuse for fans cussing out college football players and putting it on the internet. California Golden Bears head coach Tosh Lupoi looks on against the Stanford Cardinal in Berkeley, Calif., Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Getty Images But that’s where the Golden Bears find themselves while head coach Tosh Lupoi faces real questions about his job security as an embarrassing season winds down. But Cal hasn’t been competitive for over a month. They haven’t won since knocking off Virginia Tech on Oct. 10, and have lost by an average of 26.2 points over their ongoing five-game losing streak. They’ll look to snap it in their season finale next week when they host Pittsburgh. Virginia head coach Tony Elliott, left, shakes hands with California head coach Tosh Lupoi after a game at Scott Stadium in Charlottesville, Va., Nov. 14, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cal fans are not happy pic.twitter.com/Okjhl1kiUi — Stuckey (@Stuckey2) November 22, 2026 Lupoi signed a five-year, $22.6 million contract that was finalized in early October, meaning moving on would require Cal to take on a hefty buyout while the school faces a serious budget crisis. Cal’s athletic program reportedly came into the season facing a $24 million deficit and laid off some 20 people in the marketing, athletic communications and creative services departments. Stanford Cardinal players celebrate with the Stanford Axe after defeating the California Golden Bears, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Berkeley, Calif. Getty Images All while costs have risen during the transition to the Atlantic Coast Conference following the dismantling of the Pac-12 in 2024. Suffice to say, barring something drastic and unforeseen, the feeling coming out of Saturday’s loss to Stanford won’t dissipate anytime soon.

item.title: Red Wings Deal The MN Wild Trade Target to Canada
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dylan Larkin hasn’t played a game for the Detroit Red Wings since Oct. 26 against Edmonton. But the Minnesota Wild have been chasing him since the 30-year-old center asked for a trade going all the way back to May. In fact, Minnesota was on his original three-team trade list, and the only team league-wide that stayed in the Larkin hunt until the very end. Unfortunately, all that effort went for not on Sunday evening when news broke that the Team USA Olympic gold medalist has finally accepted a trade to the one place he’s been trying to avoid for months. Red Wings trade Dylan Larkin to Montreal, not the MN Wild Dylan Larkin has been traded to the Montreal Canadiens for two players, a prospect’s rights and four draft picks. Larkin accepted his fate after forfeiting $1 million in salary due to suspension. The Canadiens have acquired forward Dylan Larkin, Detroit’s second-round pick in 2028 and third-round pick in 2027 in exchange for forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, the rights to forward Michael Hage, a first-round pick in 2027, a second-round pick in 2027, a fourth-round pick in 2028 and a first-round pick in 2029. #GoHabsGo — Canadiens Montréal (@CanadiensMTL) November 22, 2026 Both teams announced the trade around 7:45 p.m. Central. Detroit gets forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault and the rights to prospect Michael Hage, plus first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick. Montreal also gets Detroit’s second-round pick in 2028 and third-round pick in 2027. Neither team announced any retained salary. Related: Reports: Injury to MN Wild Superstar Not Considered Serious only team with as much reported interest as the Wild. 10-team list , and the Wild were pushing hard to land him. Those talks dragged on, with reports last week that Detroit wasn’t negotiating in good faith with Minnesota. David Pagnotta ( The Fourth Period ) said Sunday night that the Canadiens had started warming up to moving Hage a few weeks ago, but Larkin wouldn’t waive for Montreal at the time. Michael Russo ( The Athletic ) said a Wild source had already told him the Canadiens would get Larkin by the end of the week. There ya go. Wild source said the other day Habs would get him by end of week. Larkin couldn’t sit out forever https://t.co/SndgY54obZ — Michael Russo (@RussoHockey) November 22, 2026 What Montreal gets in Dylan Larkin Obviously, the Minnesota Wild have proven early this season (with a 17-3-5 start) that they do not need Dylan Larkin to win hockey games. However, you can bet Bill Guerin will be on the phone this week trying to devise a plane to get the Central division leader over the top, come playoffs. Meanwhile, Montreal gets a center who led Detroit’s forwards in average ice time at 21:41 this season, with 2 goals, 4 assists and a plus-3 in 10 games. item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Georgia Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ATHENS, Ga. — College football’s coaches have weighed in, and their latest rankings provide another encouraging development for the Southeastern Conference. Georgia maintained the No. 1 position in Sunday’s US LBM Coaches Poll following its 34-6 victory over South Carolina. However, the Bulldogs were hardly the only SEC program making noise. Alabama, Texas and Tennessee climbed in the rankings, while Oklahoma and Missouri returned to the top 25. As a result, nine SEC teams enter Rivalry Week ranked by the coaches. Georgia remains the standard Georgia (10-1) received 60 first-place votes, keeping the Bulldogs ahead of undefeated Utah and one-loss Notre Dame. The Bulldogs have now won four consecutive games, including decisive victories over Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina. Meanwhile, Alabama climbed from No. 7 to No. 5, Texas advanced from No. 8 to No. 6 and Tennessee moved from No. 9 to No. 7. Those improvements matter as the conference prepares to determine Georgia’s opponent in Atlanta. Although the coaches poll does not control playoff selections, the rankings reflect the national perception of teams entering the regular season’s final stretch. Complete Coaches Poll Top 25 Rank Team 1 Georgia 2 Utah 3 Notre Dame 4 Miami 5 Alabama 6 Texas 7 Tennessee 8 Wake Forest 9 Texas Tech 10 UCLA 11 BYU 12 Indiana 13 Iowa 14 Oregon 15 USC 16 Arizona 17 Houston 18 Louisville 19 Ole Miss 20 Florida 21 Boise State 22 Oklahoma 23 Missouri 24 Liberty 25 Kentucky One notable difference separates the polls The coaches ranked Alabama fifth, one position ahead of Texas. The AP poll reversed that order, placing Texas fifth and Alabama sixth. Additionally, Kentucky remained in the coaches poll at No. 25 despite dropping out of the AP rankings. Ohio State experienced the opposite situation, falling out of the coaches poll while remaining No. 25 in the AP Top 25. These differences demonstrate how closely voters are evaluating programs with similar records. More importantly, the SEC’s leading teams still have opportunities to influence their postseason positions. Alabama hosts Auburn in the Iron Bowl, Texas visits Texas A&M and Tennessee travels to Vanderbilt. Meanwhile, Georgia closes its regular season against Georgia Tech. The coaches have delivered their latest assessment. Now, the SEC’s biggest rivals get the opportunity to answer on the field. item.description: CALGARY, CANADA - OCTOBER 24: Dylan Larkin #71 of the Detroit Red Wings skates against the Calgary Flames during the second period at the Scotiabank Saddledome on October 24, 2026 in Calgary, Canada. (Photo by Brett Holmes/Getty Images) Getty Images DETROIT — The Detroit Red Wings traded ex-captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster swap involving four players and six draft picks, including two first-round selections, in a deal announced by both teams on Sunday night. In acquiring Larkin, the Red Wings landed forward Kirby Dach, goalie Sam Montembeault and prospect forward Michael Hage as well as Montreal’s first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, plus a 2028 second-round selection and a 2028 fourth-rounder. Along with Larkin, Montreal acquired Detroit’s 2028 second-round pick and a third-round selection in 2027. The long-awaited trade happened between two Atlantic Division rivals and a month after the Red Wings suspended Larkin without pay. The suspension came after the player’s agent informed the team the center would no longer play for the franchise, and had grown frustrated by the Red Wings’ inability to move him months after he asked to be dealt. AP Hockey Writer John Wawrow contributed.

item.title: Let fans dream: we're happy, but chasing our dream - Gabriel Milito
item.description: Let fans dream: we're happy, but chasing our dream - Gabriel Milito Chivas put the icing on the cake of their Apertura 2026 regular season: they beat Cruz Azul, seized first place overall with 33 points, finished with the tournament’s best home record, and now await their quarterfinal series against Pachuca. The support of the Red-and-White Nation was crucial to securing their sixth home win, as the Chivas faithful never stopped cheering on Guadalajara for a single second. To overcome La Máquina, the Flock showed the solidity they aim to replicate in their first playoff tie, as Gabriel Milito noted in his post-match press conference. The Chivas coach encouraged the Red-and-White Republic to dream alongside the team as they pursue their ultimate goal. “We finished the regular season very well, winning and taking the opportunity to finish top, which is what we wanted. A new tournament begins, and we all start from zero.” “We have a tough series against Pachuca, a good team. We’ll stay humble as always, looking to compete and play our game, as the team has been doing for some time.” “In these kinds of matches, a bad 10–15 minutes can put your chances of advancing at risk; we’ll try to get as close to perfection as possible. We have to work hard and earn our place in the next round.” “It’s important to have that sense of belonging to the club, as this squad does. Those of us who arrived later are all proud to represent Chivas , and our goal is very clear.” “We know achieving that ultimate goal is no easy task, but we have to keep the dream alive and see how far we can go. Now we have to think solely and exclusively about Pachuca. Today was good; finishing first deserves a lot of credit given everything we went through during the season.” “Hopefully, we can be at our very best for what comes next, which is decisive. The series will demand that of us. The players know how important it is to push ourselves to our limits, both individually and collectively.” “It was important because it was the end of the regular season, and victory would give us not just three points but first place. Now a new tournament begins with no clear favorite; that will have to be proven once each match gets underway.” “We’re happy, but we haven’t achieved what we’re striving for.” “Let the fans dream. They’ll keep supporting the team because they see that we give everything, and we bring that competitive spirit we already have to every match. We have to dream. We’re going into this series to let our performances show what we’re capable of.” “Without humility, effort, and the right mentality, you achieve nothing in football. Those are our values, but we have to put them into practice. It will be a difficult series, but one thing is guaranteed: we’ll give it absolutely everything.” “It’s important to finish with the best defensive record and more points than everyone else. item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 22: Justice Hill #43 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates as he scores a touchdown during the first half of a football game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The early games of Week 11 are winding down. It wasn’t the prettiest slate of games, but football games and stats were produced on a field with grass or some kind of turf covering that field. We’ve seen some ugly football today, but as teams lose players to injuries and start young players for evaluation, things get ugly. Week 12 Byes None Week 12 Waiver Wire Pickups Late game update Fernando Mendoza, Raiders, QB (18%) Mendoza complete under 50% of his passes against the Broncos in Denver, but he also put up 267 yards three touchdowns and a pick-six to end the game. Three touchdown passes is pretty good, especially when you consider that Brock Bowers was unable to play. How useful he’ll be in fantasy moving forward is hard to know, but he’s proving he can put up fantasy points with some average receivers. Getting Bowers back will be huge and having Ashton Jeanty breaking off huge catch and runs doesn’t hurt either. Geno Smith, QB, Jets (18%) Smith completed 17-of-21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday’s 27-24 win over the Chargers. He remains a streaming option at quarterback despite inconsistency. Next week he faces the Dolphins, who he put up 287 yards and three touchdowns against in Week 7. Chimere Dike, WR, Tennessee Titans (13%) Dike took over the slot role in Week 11 and ended up leading the team in receptions and yards, catching 6-of-7 targets for 69 yards. It wasn’t a huge fantasy game, but if he can keep that slot job, he should be set up for a good PPR floor moving forward. Jack Bech, Raiders, WR (1%) Fernando Mendoza appears to like wide receiver Jack Bech, as he’s targeted him on 25% of his passes through his first two games. This week Bech caught 8-of-9 targets for88 yards and a touchdown. This usage comes with Brock Bowers off the field for most of the time, but I do like that Mendoza likes him and if that keeps up next week with Bowers possibly back, we may be onto something. Jacoby Brissett, QB, Ravens (21%) Justice Hill, RB, Ravens (21%) With Jacoby Brissett in as the Ravens quarterback, they are going to chuck the ball to finish out the season. In his two starts he’s thrown the ball 49 and 37 times. This isn’t your Lamar Jackson Ravens anymore, as he attempted 20, 20, 31, and 25 passes in his four full starts this year. Derrick Henry needs the threat of Jackson taking off as a runner to keep teams honest. Without that the Ravens aren’t going to force the run like they once did. More passing is great for Zay Flowers and good for Brissett and running back Justice Hill. item.title: Player grades: SGA-less Thunder punt in 123-113 loss to Heat
item.description: Eventually scratched from his first game of the season, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's absence turned this into a skippable watch at worst and background noise at best. The two-time MVP winner went through his pregame warmups, but that was it in his sole visit to one of the most historic gyms in the NBA. The Oklahoma City Thunder stomached through a 123-113 loss to the Miami Heat . They trailed the entire night and by as many as 20 points. Before the cross-conference matchup even happened, the Thunder punted it on the front end of road back-to-back. Not only was Gilgeous-Alexander, but so were Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, Alex Caruso and plenty of other names. To twist the knife, Aday Mara was a very-late scratch, too. Sure, the Heat were without Giannis Antetokounmpo, but it was a matchup of their B squad butting heads with OKC's C squad. The only Opening Night starter who was suited up for the Thunder was Isaiah Hartenstein. This is the NBA reality they're in right now with their long list of injuries. Any hopes of a miraculous win popped like a balloon. Not even three minutes in, the Thunder were in an 11-2 deficit. Klay Thompson grilled them from the outside — ala 2016. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain tried their best collective carry job, but just didn't have the scoring superpowers to do so. The Thunder were in a 36-24 deficit after the first quarter. Finally, the Thunder enjoyed some outside shooting luck. Kenrich Williams drained a 3-pointer to make it a single-digit contest. But anytime it felt like OKC was about to go on a run, the Heat answered back with timely outside jumpers. That was the game's flow throughout the first half. The Thunder had 30 points in the second quarter. They entered halftime with a 67-54 deficit. Bam Adebayo balled out as he flirted with a triple-double. It was the first time this year that he enjoyed first-option hoops. Alas, the second half brought zero intrigue. It was mostly the same as both teams played it out of necessity. Williams had some nice scoring plays, but made costly mistakes as he was asked to be one of their top players. Josh Dix also showed flashes as OKC's best two-way guy with outside makes and good defensive energy. Mitchell had an epic four-point play. But yeah, that's really it. We're really grasping at straws to find meaty thoughts on this inevitable loss once Gilgeous-Alexander was ruled out. The Thunder had 26 points in the third quarter, but the Heat continued to stiff-arm them on the scoreboard. At that juncture in the game, OKC was in a 95-80 hole. Remember when it had a several-year run as one of the league's top defenses? If you stayed through this, you're a real NBA trooper. Enjoy whatever online brownie points you can get. The skeleton Thunder gave you every incentive to tune into the NFL Sunday slate instead. The fourth quarter was forgettable as the game got out of hand. OKC put up 33 points in the final frame to pretty up the final score of this wire-to-wire defeat.

item.title: Ravens Star Silenced for Joke, Even as Team’s Season Collapses
item.description: Jul 29, 2026; Ownings Mills, MD, USA; Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey (44) during practice at the Under Armour Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images Marlon Humphrey made a joke on his own podcast. Asked what Baltimore is best at making, he named the Star-Spangled Banner and National Bohemian beer, then added, “They’re best at making criminals.” It was a throwaway line in a casual conversation. He immediately noted it would get cut. The next day, he apologized, pointing out that he’s spent his whole career in the city, has welcomed a son there, and invests locally. The Ravens treated it like a major offense. Coach Jesse Minter sent him home from the facility and made him a healthy scratch for Sunday’s game against the Panthers. One-game deactivation, still gets paid, conversations “personal and private.” Officially it’s about removing a distraction while the team tries to snap a five-game losing streak. That framing doesn’t hold up. The Ravens are 4-6 and sliding. They’re already missing other defensive starters. Humphrey has started every game this season and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the roster. His recent play has been inconsistent, yet the organization has kept him in the lineup and at the top of the cornerback pay scale. A light podcast joke produced an immediate benching . The actual losses have not. Mayor Brandon Scott and others called the comment unacceptable and the apology insufficient. Public criticism is part of the job. What’s harder to defend is a struggling franchise choosing this moment for a public stand. When a team is getting beaten week after week, deactivating a starter over an offhand remark looks more like virtue signaling than football discipline. It signals seriousness without fixing the problems that actually cost games. Humphrey is expected back next week. The Ravens’ larger issues—offensive inconsistency, defensive holes, a losing streak—will still be there. Silencing a player for a joke doesn’t change any of that. It just gives a flailing organization something to point to while the losses continue.

item.title: Raiders show heart but cannot capitalize on opportunities in loss to Broncos
item.description: Nov 22, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Las Vegas Raiders tight end Ian Thomas (80) celebrates after catching a nineteen-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Fernando Mendoza (not pictured) against the Denver Broncos during the third quarter at Empower Field at Mile High. DENVER—What was looking like a day to remember for Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders quickly soured in the thin Denver air. Even on a day with several positive developments, mistakes undid the Raiders in their 38-24 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. The early schedule for Mendoza’s first career starts has been far from a cakewalk, but the first overall pick has done well in cementing himself as the starting quarterback of the present and future in Las Vegas. Against Denver, Mendoza showed improvement over his first start against the Seattle Seahawks, throwing for 267 yards and three touchdowns. With no Brock Bowers in the lineup as he recovers from his ankle injury he sustained against Seattle, Mendoza found excellent chemistry with Ashton Jeanty (five receptions for a game-high 90 yards and a touchdown) and Jack Bech (game-high eight receptions for a career-high 88 yards and a touchdown). The improved passing attack also coincided with one of the best rushing days the Raiders have had since Week One against the Miami Dolphins, with Jeanty, Mendoza and Mike Washington Jr. collectively averaging six yards per carry for 143 total rushing yards. However, the issues with the offense are not yet completely fixed, highlighted by Mendoza’s interception to Ja’Quan McMillian that iced the game in favor of the Broncos. The offensive line struggled once again to keep pressure from getting to Mendoza, as the rookie was sacked five times for a total of 11 in the first two starts. The rookie also saw six passes get batted down at the line of scrimmage. Another point of emphasis was Mendoza not yet getting chemistry down with his veteran receivers. Despite 15 combined targets going towards Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor, they only recorded three receptions between them, indicating the need to continue developing the execution on offense. However, Nailor did have two touchdowns that were wiped out by penalties, so there is at least something to build off of. Meanwhile, the defense continued to have its struggles, particularly in containing the run. Not to be outdone by Mendoza, Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman solidified his place in the backfield with a tremendous performance. Leading Denver with 24 carries, Coleman rumbled for 111 yards and three rushing touchdowns in one of the best outings by a rookie this season. Also doing the Raiders in were nine penalties worth 63 yards, as well as two blocked punts from AJ Cole. With the Raiders sitting at 4-7, they will need to make a mad dash to remain in the hunt for a playoff spot, and the newly-flexed Sunday Night Football matchup against the Cleveland Browns next week has become a must-win to have any postseason aspirations headin

item.title: Breaking: Dylan Larkin Traded to Montreal Canadiens for Three Player Haul
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Red Wings have finally said enough is enough. Six months after Dylan Larkin requested a trade out of Detroit, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has granted the former Red Wings captain’s request. Larkin is going to the Montreal Canadiens alongside a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round selection from the Red Wings in exchange for goaltender Sam Montembault, forward Kirby Dach, and top prospect center Michael Hage . Hage is a teammate of current Red Wings prospect JP Hurlbert at the University of Michigan. Also coming back to Detroit in the trade are conditional first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick, and a 2028 fourth-rounder. While the Canadiens were not on Larkin’s official 10-team trade list, after losing over a million dollars in the three weeks since deciding he would no longer play for the Red Wings, apparently Detroit was able to convince Larkin to waive his no-trade clause to move north of the border. Packing his bags for Detroit meanwhile, Dach has been playing primarily on the Canadiens third line, with two goals and six assists so far this season while playing on a one year, 3.6 million dollar contract. Montembault is currently on injured reserve , having last played in March of this year. The 30-year-old veteran netminder has played 232 games in the NHL, primarily with the Canadiens and is signed to a 3.15 million dollar AAV contract that expires later this year. DHN will have a story grading the trade posted later. Related Headlines Where is Red Wings Fire? item.title: Red Wings trade Dylan Larkin to Canadiens in NHL blockbuster
item.description: Simon Nemec #71 of the Calgary Flames skates against Dylan Larkin #71 of the Detroit Red Wings in Calgary, Alberta, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. Dylan Larkin finally has his landing spot. The Red Wings are trading their ex-captain to the Canadiens for three players and four future draft picks, the team announced on Sunday. Forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault and the rights to forward Michael Hage are heading to Detroit along with conditional first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-rounder. Simon Nemec #71 of the Calgary Flames skates against Dylan Larkin #71 of the Detroit Red Wings in Calgary, Alberta, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. NHLI via Getty Images Detroit is also sending its 2028 second-round pick and 2027 third-rounder. The trade is a long time coming after Larkin very publicly requested a trade ahead of the season. He was stripped of his captaincy and has forfeited over $1 million after being suspended without pay on Oct. 29. Larkin, who won a gold medal with Team USA at the 2026 Olympics, reportedly cited the Red Wings’ 10-year playoff drought as a major reason for requesting the trade. It’s the latest blockbuster deal in a stretch that’s been full of them for the American Olympic roster. Connor Hellebuyck was suspended to begin the season before the Jets traded him to the Devils last month. Brady Tkachuk requested a trade from the Senators and was dealt to the Panthers before the season started. Reigning MVP Nikita Kucherov has also requested a trade, though he remains playing on the Lightning’s top line and it’s unclear if a deal is coming.

item.title: Broncos’ Sean Payton pulls off classy postgame move in honor of Tom Jackson
item.description: Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Broncos’ Sean Payton pulls off classy postgame move in honor of Tom Jackson appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Sean Payton ’s Denver Broncos are 8-2 after a 38-24 home win over the Las Vegas Raiders that saw offensive coordinator Davis Webb’s unit come to life on a day when franchise star Tom Jackson’s passing was announced, leading to a ‘Jacked Up’ ESPN tribute . The Broncos’ offense starred in the win as Jonah Coleman reached a Clinton Portis pantheon at the running back position. Following the game, Payton had a special tribute locked and loaded for Jackson. “He got a game ball tonight, his family…Part of the rich history, obviously, tough loss for everyone,” Payton said, clearly emotional over the loss of the Broncos and ESPN legend. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The #Broncos gave a game ball to the family of the late Tom Jackson. Here’s Sean Payton on Jackson postgame 👇🏼 pic.twitter.com/xp6i4x1nUN — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 23, 2026 Jackson was a big-time playmaker with the Broncos, intercepting 20 passes and recovering eight fumbles in 14 seasons with the franchise. Denver’s Vance Joseph-led defense didn’t have its best day against the Raiders, giving up nearly 370 yards to its rookie Fernando Mendoza-led attack, but the offense picked them up. QB Bo Nix had 225 yards passing with one touchdown and one interception, while Coleman rushed for 111 yards on 24 carries with three touchdowns. The Broncos missed out on key opportunities in the first half as Troy Franklin botched a Nix deep ball that had six points written all over it. The second half was better as the Broncos cashed in their opportunities, cruising to a much-needed division win. Coach Payton and his franchise got the opportunity to learn about a true Broncos and NFL legend on Sunday, but not under the circumstances that they wanted to hear. The Broncos’ division title hopes remain intact heading into Week 12 against the Steelers as fans continue to mourn Jackson’s passing, and to remember his timeless contributions. item.title: COP31: Onuigbo tasks legislators on climate laws, funding
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The President of GLOBE Legislators International, Rt. Hon. Sir Sam Ifeanyi Onuigbo, has urged parliamentarians across the world to translate international climate agreements into enforceable national laws, backed by adequate funding and effective oversight. Onuigbo said international climate agreements would achieve little unless national parliaments incorporated decisions reached at United Nations climate conferences into domestic legislation and ensured their implementation. He made the call at the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) COP31 Parliamentary Meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, where he highlighted the role of legislators in ensuring that commitments reached at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conferences of the Parties (COPs) produced tangible results at the national level. In a statement made available to journalists in Gombe on Saturday, the former member of the House of Representatives said parliamentarians must deploy their constitutional powers of lawmaking, budgetary appropriation and oversight to ensure governments implement international climate commitments. Drawing on his legislative experience, Onuigbo recalled that his participation in the GLOBE COP21 Legislators Summit in Paris influenced his decision to sponsor Nigeria’s Climate Change Act. He argued that without the necessary legislative backing, negotiations and agreements reached at international climate conferences could fail to translate into practical outcomes. “After all the contributions here, if they are not brought down into laws for implementation, it becomes an exercise in futility,” he said. Onuigbo described parliamentary action as central to bridging the gap between international climate negotiations and domestic implementation. He stressed that legislators must ensure that agreements reached at COP meetings were reflected in national laws, budgetary allocations and effective government oversight. Describing the deliberations at the Antalya meeting as detailed and incisive, he said their impact would ultimately depend on the ability of parliamentarians to translate the discussions into actionable legislation. The GLOBE Legislators president also commended the National Council on Climate Change, its leadership under Dr Majekodunmi, researchers and other stakeholders for their contributions to the development of the Host Country Approval Criteria for Carbon Market Activities in Nigeria and the country’s broader climate change efforts. He also acknowledged President Bola Tinubu’s role in Nigeria’s climate change efforts. “Above all, I want to thank President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who has exercised admirable leadership in ensuring that the climate journey remains steady and very successful,” he said. Onuigbo was inaugurated as President of GLOBE Legislators at the United Kingdom Parliament on June 24, 2026. item.title: $1 of GPT-5.1 tokens finds new ways around China’s Great Firewall
item.description: Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hypersc

item.title: Tinubu’s reforms may be difficult to sustain without re-election — Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said it would be difficult to sustain and stabilise President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms if he fails to secure re-election in 2027. Wike said the initial challenges associated with the removal of petrol subsidy were temporary, arguing that Tinubu should be allowed to complete the foundation he had laid for Nigeria’s economic recovery and prosperity. The minister spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at St Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State. He said Nigeria had been facing the threat of economic collapse before Tinubu assumed office, describing the president as courageous for taking difficult decisions. “This country was on the verge of collapse. But by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” Wike said. “And that is why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. He has laid his foundation; now it’s time for prosperity. If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done.” Wike cited what he described as improved stability in the university system, noting that strikes by lecturers over unpaid entitlements, which frequently disrupted academic calendars in the past, were no longer a recurring feature under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners previously encountered in accessing their entitlements, arguing that decisions taken by the president had helped address some of the country’s longstanding challenges. The FCT minister urged Nigerians across religious divides to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, insisting that the president’s campaign would accommodate Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters. The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes,” he said. Wike also dismissed claims of religious imbalance in appointments under the Tinubu administration, insisting that Christians had enjoyed greater representation in the current government than in previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” he said. The minister, during the service, announced a donation of N100 million to the church on behalf of the Rainbow Coalition, his friends and associates. item.title: NELFUND considers increase in ₦20,000 student upkeep
item.description: …Sawyer says allowance under review, hints at possible changes By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) is considering an increase in its ₦20,000 monthly upkeep allowance for students amid concerns that rising living costs have reduced its purchasing power. The Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on TVC’s Beyond the Headlines, saying the allowance was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new amount or timeline for any adjustment, Sawyer confirmed that the possibility of an increase was being considered. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The proposed review comes amid complaints by students that the current allowance is inadequate to meet the rising costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic needs. Sawyer, however, said any increase would have to take into account the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for all eligible beneficiaries. “What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” he said. Beyond the proposed review, the NELFUND chief disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was considering an intervention to provide students with more substantial financial support to help them complete their academic programmes. He did not provide details of the proposed intervention, including its scope, funding or implementation timeline. “I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” Sawyer said. He also hinted that changes could be introduced in the future, although he gave no definite commitment on when the review would be concluded. “I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added. NELFUND’s proposed review comes as the Federal Government’s student loan scheme continues to expand, with millions of applications received from students seeking financial assistance for tertiary education. According to figures provided by the fund, it has disbursed ₦180.5 billion in upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024, while another ₦194.7 billion has been paid to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees. The combined disbursement of approximately ₦375.2 billion underscores the scale of the programme, which is intended to reduce financial barriers to tertiary education and help students remain in school. The fund has also recorded more than 2.5 million applications and about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions. Despite the programme’s expansion, the adequacy of the monthly upkeep allowance remains a concern for beneficiaries who depend on it to meet their daily expenses. item.title: Atletico Madrid beat Getafe 3-0 to keep pressure on Barcelona, Real Madrid
item.description: Atletico Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe in La Liga on Sunday. Diego Simeone’s side, third, are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off second-place Real Madrid, who both won earlier this weekend. Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julian Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital. Alex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sorloth. “I think the team had a very good, serious game, in defence and attack,” Atletico playmaker Baena told Movistar. “We are focused on our own work, not looking at what Barcelona and Madrid are doing, and that suits us best.” The Rojiblancos moved ahead after 10 minutes, with Alvarez teeing up Baena on the edge of the box to drill home low and hard at the near post. Getafe goalkeeper David Soria saved well from Alvarez and David Hancko but was at fault for Atletico’s second goal. Soria missed his punch from Alvarez’s corner and United States international Cardoso turned home with his knee from point-blank range. Baena smashed over a fine chance for the third after Pablo Barrios played him in behind. Soria denied Baena in the second half and Lee Kang-in fired over as Atletico continued to control the game and defended solidly to keep Getafe, 17th, at bay. Atletico substitute Sorloth should have scored with a few minutes remaining but powered an effort straight at Soria. item.title: Watch live on Nov. 23: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
item.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

item.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims. The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday. After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament. Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals. With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998. “It’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way, so I’m really proud,” Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year. “I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I’m playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I’ve been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament. A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles. But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals. He lost in the season-ender’s final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one. Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings. – Topsy-turvy – The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three. The first set of Alcaraz’s semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week. Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold. Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand. Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1. item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state. Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door. “Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said. The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights. “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added. ﻿ Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi , who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes. The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo. Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country. However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots. Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race.
