item.title: What's next for NASA interstellar Voyager 1 probe after passing 1 light-day from Earth?
item.description: null Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft. Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2 , launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s. Voyager 1's faster path out of the solar system brought it to one light-day in distance on Wednesday (Nov. 18), while Voyager 2 — which took a slightly slower track to see Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — will reach a light-day of distance in 2035. So what's next for the two Voyager spacecraft as they reach further into interstellar space? Exploring afar Interstellar space, which is the area where the sun's constant stream of solar particles within the heliopause gives way to the physics of interstellar space, has been a valuable harvest for both Voyagers. Voyager 1 crossed interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to get data, while Voyager 2 has done the same since November 2018. "Current science is continuing our investigation on magnetic field strength and direction, plasma density, and energetic particle detection. What is important is to measure how these phenomena change as the spacecraft travels further away from the sun," Suzanne Dodd, project manager for the Voyager missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), told Space.com in an email. Added to that will be the Voyagers' examinations of plasma and magnetic fields nearby the spacecraft, and a focus on any "solar effects" such as shocks or pressure fronts, added JPL project scientist Linda Spilker in an email. "Key Voyager science going forward includes observing the extent to which our sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1," Spilker continued. "Where does the sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may last long enough to answer that question." The team also wants to watch the magnetic field around the spacecraft continue to change direction from the sun, to interstellar space, Spilker noted. That finding was not expected when the Voyagers launched, so scientists are curious to know more — as long as the spacecraft can last, that is. The locations of Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 beyond the boundary of our solar system. (Image credit: NASA, ESA, and Z. Levay (STScI)) Power management Each Voyager continues to lose 4 watts of power a year; their launch power was 470 watts in 1977, and the nuclear power source continues to dwindle, requiring harder choices as the missions approach their 50th years of operations. Instruments have had to be shut off, and both the spacecraft were directed to perform a "Big Bang" of power redistribution earlier this year to preserve as much

item.title: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after attackers compromise customer accounts
item.description: Transport for London (TfL) has copped to another cybersecurity breach, this time involving the account details of around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers. The capital's transport operator told The Register it first became aware something was amiss on November 16, when Oyster photocard customers started receiving emails asking them to create accounts they already had. The emails came from TfL's own systems, the transport body confirmed, but were generated as a result of the compromise. "We immediately took the TfL photocard website down while this was being investigated," said Shashi Verma, TfL's director of technology strategy and revenue. "The protection of personal information is a priority for us, and I apologize to our customers affected by this incident." TfL reckons its speedy response spared a considerable number of customers from having their details compromised. The transport operator says it has since contained the incident and contacted those potentially affected, though it is rather more forthcoming about what the hackers didn't get their hands on than what they did. TfL says no passwords, bank or payment card details, or customer journey information were compromised. It also believes the names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were unaffected. Among those whose accounts may have been compromised are holders of Zip Oyster cards – issued to children as young as five – as well as students, apprentices, care leavers, veterans, and Londoners aged 60 and over. Despite the assurances about passwords, TfL says it will ask all photocard customers to change theirs, along with their security questions and answers. Those in the habit of recycling passwords across multiple websites are being advised to change them elsewhere, too. TfL says it has yet to find any evidence that the compromised data has been used and has notified the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO). The transport operator hasn't disclosed how the perpetrators got into its systems. Existing photocards will still let holders through the ticket barriers, though anyone needing to renew one or check their journey history will have to contact TfL's customer services team while the website is out of action . There's no word yet on when it'll be back. "We hope to restore the affected website services as quickly as possible," Verma said. TfL should be well versed in dealing with data breaches by now. In March, the transport operator told The Register it had notified more than 7 million customers following its September 2024 cyberattack. The hackers had accessed systems holding customers' names, email addresses, and home addresses, while around 5,000 customers were contacted as a priority because their bank account details may also have been compromised. Two teenagers were subsequently charged in connection with the attack, which authorities linked to the notorious Scattered Spider cybercrime crew. item.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
item.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. The Empty Chair Nobody Notices This year’s theme for International Men’s Day, celebrated on November 19th, is “The Future Is Everyone.” While this theme may seem straightforward, it invites us to explore the true meaning of “everyone.” Working in corporate communications at the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria (CIPM) has heightened my awareness of how easily we categorise people based on their roles: leaders, em

item.title: Sticky note on monitor provided keys to the company’s kingdom
item.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we talk smack about organizations that have smacked themselves down by practicing poor security hygiene. This week's story involves everyone's favorite low-tech password manager: the sticky note. Our terrifying tale comes courtesy of Christian Espinosa, a certified penetration tester with over 30 years of experience and the CEO of Blue Goat Cyber , a security company. Espinosa shared an experience where critical credentials were right out in the open for any person in the office to see. During a walkthrough of a client's office, he noticed a password written on a sticky note that was taped to an employee's monitor. While writing down your password and placing it in a physically secure paper notebook might be ok, taping it to the computer is definitely not. "Before I get my fingers on any system, I first walk the physical area that the system is located in — attackers do that when they're looking at a target too," Espinosa explained. “Physical security vulnerabilities are neglected much more often than technical security vulnerabilities and firms invest in firewalls where a sticky note is placed 3 feet from the front door." Espinosa took a photo of the sticky note and immediately tried logging into that employee's account. Success. Then, he tried the very same password on the VPN, which apparently had been maintained by that employee. Once he connected to the VPN, Espinosa had full access to the company network and all of its shared drives. He opened a shared drive that this employee had access to and there was an HR folder with all kinds of personally identifiable information (PII) about employees, including home addresses, driver's licenses, and scanned W-4 forms. There were even spreadsheets that listed everyone's salaries. The employee account also had access to a document that contained a list of internal server names and the names of the people in charge of each server (great for phishing). Another document had instructions for how to log into the accounting server specifically. The accounting server was a particular treasure trove of client information. On that server, Espinosa found a folder with vendor banking information, invoices, and payment records. "At that point, a password I had read from a sticky note during a walk-through had taken me from one desk to information that could have been used for payroll fraud, identity theft, or vendor-payment fraud," Espinosa said. After getting access to all this information, the pen tester presented his findings to the client. They quickly disabled the rogue account and started reviewing VPN access logs to see who else might have gotten into the network. They then searched the office to see if anyone else was exposing a password on a sticky note. Finally, they tightened permissions on the HR and accounting shares so that only people who really needed access to that data could get in. The lessons here are pretty obvious. item.title: Burna Boy, Asake & Seyi Vibez Bring Afrobeats to the World of GTA VI
item.description: From left: Nigerian artists Asake, Seyi Vibez, and Burna Boy, whose songs appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. How else could Grand Theft Auto VI begin than with Nigerian artists featured in the music lineup of the biggest video game release of the year? As players around the world finally step into Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated open-world action-adventure title, Burna Boy , Asake , and Seyi Vibez are making sure Nigerian music is front and centre on the virtual streets of Vice City and the wider state of Leonida. Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) officially arrives today, Thursday, 19 November 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V first hit consoles. Developed and published by Rockstar Games, the open-world action-adventure game follows dual protagonists Jason and Lucia across the sun-soaked, neon-lit state of Leonida—a fictional take on Florida that brings players back to Vice City in the franchise’s largest map yet. Music has always been at the heart of the Grand Theft Auto universe, where players tune into curated in-game radio stations while driving or walking around town, and this sixth instalment takes African soundscapes seriously. At the centre of the Nigerian presence is AfroBank FM, a dedicated African music radio station inside Grand Theft Auto VI that is co-hosted by Grammy winner Burna Boy—credited on-air simply as Burna—alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax , who goes by Palmsy. Curated to spotlight everything from 20th-century African classics to contemporary Afrobeats, amapiano, and 3-step, the station features Asake’s 2022 hit “ Joha ” from his debut album Mr Money With The Vibe , as well as “ Giza “, the 2023 collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez from Burna Boy’s seventh studio album I Told Them …. Alongside those tracks, Burna Boy also appears on the game’s official companion soundtrack album, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, with his original song “ Bigger ” sitting on a 34-track roster that includes Travis Scott , Cardi B , Dua Lipa , SZA , Tame Impala , and Lana Del Rey . The African representation on AfroBank FM stretches beyond Nigeria too, sharing airwaves with Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor on “ Gye Wani ” and South African stars DJ Lag , Robot Boii , and Kamo Mphela on “ Shay’sana “. With players able to listen to Leonida’s terrestrial radio stations both in vehicles and on foot through in-game headphones, millions of gamers worldwide are now cruising through Vice City with Burna Boy on the mic and Asake and Seyi Vibez on heavy rotation. The post Burna Boy, Asake & Seyi Vibez Bring Afrobeats to the World of GTA VI appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Uncensored AI models are thriving on code hosting platforms
item.description: Uncensored large language models (ULLMs) capable of producing harmful content are readily available at popular model-hosting websites, calling into question AI industry commitments to safety. Researchers affiliated with University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in the US and Nanyang Technological University in Singapore have analysed 22,096 ULLMs collected from five major LLM hosting platforms. As described in their paper , "Characterizing the Ecosystem of Open-Source Uncensored Large Language Models: Supply Chain, Governance, and Risks," authors Zilong Lin, Zichuan Li, Xiaojing Liao, and XiaoFeng Wang found that uncensored LLMs are easy to obtain from hosting platforms like US-based Hugging Face, Kaggle, and John Snow Labs, and China-based OpenCSG and ModelScope. What's more, these unrestrained models have been deployed through applications, GitHub projects, and model routing platforms like Open Router, and users of those apps or services may not be aware of the nature of the underlying LLM. "Uncensored LLMs generally refer to LLMs whose content filtering or refusal safeguards are absent, removed, or weakened, allowing them to respond to requests that aligned models may refuse," the paper explains. Zilong Lin, lead author and assistant professor of computer science at the University of Missouri-Kansas City, told The Register that open source LLM hosting platforms like Hugging Face play a similar role to code hosting services like GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg in the open source community by enabling sharing, modification, and redistribution of code artifacts. "However, unlike traditional software, whose behavior can often be examined through source code analysis, the safety alignment of LLMs is difficult to assess directly from their model files," Lin explained. "Evaluating whether an LLM has adequate safety safeguards typically requires deploying the model and testing its responses to potentially harmful prompts, which involves substantial computational and financial costs." Lin said this makes the identification and assessment of LLM safety particularly challenging, particularly given the large number of models available. That's why he and his colleagues chose to study the space through publicly available model metadata. Even popular commercial LLMs that are purportedly "aligned" – to some standard not everyone accepts – may respond to prompts with content deemed harmful. The US Government Accountability Office just released a report that found Claude, Grok, ChatGPT, and Gemini can be coaxed to provide information that would help with the planning of a terror attack. To highlight the consequences of AI advice, the GAO points to news reports indicating that generative AI helped enable the creation of an explosive device in a January 2025 attack on a Las Vegas hotel and the planning of a February 2026 mass shooting in British Columbia, Canada. item.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
item.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. item.title: Google continues model chemistry experiment with Neon
item.description: Google periodically tables new AI models named after elements, and its latest offering has the noble name "Neon." "Engineered for long-running agent workflows, Neon sustains performance through complex, tool-heavy tasks end-to-end — whether running standalone or acting as a fast, high-judgment Orchestrator directing parallel Hydrogen subagents in Google Antigravity," explained Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, in a blog post . Neon emerged after Google last week emitted Hydrogen , after delivering Carbon two weeks earlier and wafting Argon out the door in late September. Unlike OpenAI's celestial more intuitive model naming scheme – Astra, Sol, Luna, and Terra – which maps celestial position to capability, Google's chemical soup doesn't suggest a specific hierarchy. To judge by price , Carbon or Argon would be Google's top tier model, based on non-discounted price that takes effect next month, each priced at $4/M input tokens, $20/M output. The Chocolate Factory refers to Carbon as "Our most capable reasoning model" while Argon is "Our efficient Gemini 4 frontier reasoning model … with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon across complex coding, agentic, math, and science tasks." Yet Neon, the latest element in the mix, surpasses both in Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index , scoring 61 compared to Carbon at 60, Hydrogen at 54, and Argon at 50. At the same time, Neon costs less, at $3/M input tokens and $15/M output. That favorable pricing is all the more surprising in light of Google's willingness, as of two days ago , to let users of its Gemini services opt out of generative AI model training without losing their chat histories. Kavukcuoglu evidently recognizes the need to clarify its model rankings, an issue addressed in a blog post section titled "Where Neon sits in the Gemini 4 family." "While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency," he explains. "Neon delivers frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently." That may not really clarify which model is appropriate for which task and frankly Google is fine with that. As noted, Google Antigravity comes with an Orchestrator that decides how to spend your money for you by swapping models on the fly. As the company describes it, a developer might start a task using Carbon, which would write a plan, and hand the task off to Hydrogen to benefit from its token thrift. Antigravity does support model pinning , for those who know what they want. But Google, like other companies exploring model routing and orchestration, is fine with developers delegating decisions that affect billing to their trustworthy service provider. ®

item.title: The Future Awards Africa (TFAA) celebrates 20 Years of African Excellence with Historic Awards Ceremony
item.description: A historic hosting line-up spanning five African countries and a first-of-its-kind AI assistant named Infinity set the stage for a distinctive celebration as The Future Awards Africa (TFAA) marked its 20th edition on Saturday, 14 November 2026. Held at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, the ceremony brought together young achievers, industry leaders and public figures to celebrate two decades of recognizing African excellence. Themed “ Celebrating the Redefiners: Africa’s AI Generation,” the evening honoured young Africans aged 18 to 35 across 26 categories, including technology and innovation, entrepreneurship, governance, music, film, literature, advocacy, sports and fashion. Their achievements formed the heart of a milestone edition that celebrated the platform’s legacy while embracing new possibilities for its stage. The event was hosted by Nigerian actress and trained lawyer Genoveva Umeh; Claudia Naisabwa , a Kenyan media personality and host; Priscilla Kayira , a Malawian radio broadcaster and television personality; Resego Motlhokathari , a television and radio host from Botswana; and Idris Sultan , a Tanzanian actor and former Big Brother Africa winner. Together, the five hosts gave the anniversary celebration a distinctly continental presence. Bringing different voices, personalities and perspectives to the proceedings, the line-up reflected the reach of an awards platform whose story has grown alongside the generations of young Africans it recognises. The hosts also shared the spotlight with Infinity , an AI assistant that introduced another dimension to the evening. With a distinct voice, quick wit, and playful responses, Infinity engaged with the hosts, drawing laughter and creating unexpected, exciting moments throughout the ceremony. Its appearance offered an exciting glimpse into how artificial intelligence is influencing not only the way people work and create, but also how audiences experience entertainment. Sharp Band and the Loud Urban Choir also entertained guests with captivating musical performances, adding to the evening’s celebratory atmosphere. At the heart of the celebration were the winners and the work that earned them recognition. Nora Awolowo received the Prize for Young Person of the Year, Teniola Aladese won the Prize for Acting, and Olamidun Ogundoyin took home the Prize for Entrepreneurship. Pastor Jerry Uchechukwu Eze , who was represented at the ceremony by media personality Hero Daniels , received the Prize for Service to Young People. The ceremony welcomed representatives of distinguished public figures, including Hon. Mobolaji Abubakre Ogunlende, Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, who represented the Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu . item.title: International Men’s Day: Six Films That Explore the Vulnerable Side of Men
item.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Where does responsibility begin, and where does it end? Do men matter? Do their feelings matter? The theme for this year’s International Men’s Day is “The Future Is For Everyone.” For that, here are some movies that explore and illuminate the complexities of masculinity: The Pursuit of Happyness This classic film reveals the vulnerability often hidden behind male perseverance. Will Smith ’s portrayal of Chris Gardner challenges the stoic notion of manhood by showing fatherhood as both an act of love and endurance. Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. Through this film, Kevin Hart shares his vision of what it means to be a man and a father. Adolescence Adolescence examines how boys internalise distorted notions of strength and freedom, and how escaping them demands emotional awareness. The film reveals the journey of a young boy on the brink of adulthood, revealing the pressures of identity and self-definition. There is a lot to unpack from Stephen Graham’ s Adolescence about what it means to be a father and a child. King Richard A faction. In the narrative, King Richard shares the stories of Serena and Venus Williams , highlighting discipline and belief as fundamental expressions of a father’s love. item.title: GTA VI didn't break the internet, thanks to 'stupid DNS tricks'
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI may put a dent in global productivity today but the game didn’t break the internet. For those unfamiliar, GTA VI is the first new instalment of the mega-hit game in 13 years and it is nearly impossible to understate the excitement surrounding its release. Anecdotal evidence suggests fans of the game may today report they suddenly feel unfit to perform paid work. Developer Rockstar Games allowed Xbox and PlayStation owners to pay for and download the 200GB-plus game on November 10, before play commenced on the 19 th . Millions took advantage of the chance to download the game, creating just the sort of internet traffic event that regional internet registry the Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre (RIPE NCC) can observe with its RIPE Atlas internet measurement network. RIPE data scientist Emile Aben, with help from staffers Alun Davies and James Cowie, went looking for GTA-related traffic and found some interesting patterns . Aben observed that traffic to PlayStations mostly came from content delivery networks operated by AWS and Fastly. Microsoft relied on Fastly for over half of traffic flowing to Xboxes and used Akamai too, but eschewed AWS's CloudFront. The data scientist observed heavy use of “GeoDNS,” a technique that returns different IP addresses for a single domain request, depending on a user’s location. DNS’s designers didn’t intend that. Indeed, the RIPE trio point out that Paul Vixie, the computer scientist who earned his place in the Internet Hall of Fame for massive contributions to the DNS system, regarded things like GeoDNS as “stupid DNS tricks.” Whatever you think of GeoDNS, the RIPE researchers found that folks who were likely downloading GTA VI from Los Angeles, Tokyo, and Istanbul were each directed to different sites. Their probe of a network in Shanghai, China, found “a very distinct long lookup-chain with a hostname that is associated with the Alibaba Cloud in the end that maps to six different IP addresses.” “This hints at specialised treatment for some countries/regions,” Aben wrote. He also noted that Internet Exchange Points, the interconnect facilities that network operators use to exchange traffic and shorten paths, had to cope with record traffic during the download period – and seem to have handled the load. Aben thinks the GTA VI download program offers a useful lesson. “DNS helps steer each player towards a download server, while multiple CDNs share the work of delivering the files,” he wrote. “That distribution matters beyond gaming. On the open Internet, game downloads share routers and link capacity with all kinds of other traffic, including critical services.” “Keeping downloads local helps leave capacity on long-distance links free for other uses, making that enormous demand manageable.” ®

item.title: South Korea tries to out exam cheats with Extreme Emergency smartphone alert
item.description: At 08:30 on Thursday morning every powered-on mobile phone in South Korea blared out an Extreme Emergency Alert tone for 10.5 seconds – but the nation was at peace, with no major natural disasters occurring. The extreme emergency South Korea hoped to avoid was cheating in the annual College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), an exam that over half a million people sit in the hope of securing admission to their preferred university. This year, around a third of those applicants are repeating the test after their previous effort didn’t get them the result they wanted. CSAT involves five separate examinations staged in a single day. Participants can only bring pencils to the test. Smartphones or any sort of tech is strictly forbidden. Which is why Korean authorities used the national alert system on the day of CSAT, because if the 40dB tone sounded in an exam centre, it could indicate a student had deliberately or inadvertently tried to bring a smartphone – perhaps as an exam aide. Korean media report the 08:30 alert turned up nine phones. Authorities will send a second alert tone at an unspecified time later in the day to again smoke out any surreptitious smartphones. It’s not possible to opt out of the alerts, one reason a concerned netizen has used the Android issue tracker to suggest sending alerts to detect exam cheats could be an abuse of the emergency alert system that Google might want to do something about. South Korea sends a lot of emergency alerts, for matters such as helping to find missing persons or to warn of dangerous weather. It’s not uncommon to receive several in a single day. Authorities also gave advance notice of the CSAT alerts, which will not, therefore, cause panic on the streets of Seoul or Busan. CSAT day is, however, a serious occasion. Some businesses open late so test-takers can get to their exams without having to battle peak hour traffic. Those measures are arguably less disruptive than the widespread internet outages that some states in India impose on major exam days. An alleged leak of one Indian exam paper saw the nation’s tech regulator ban messaging service Telegram in the country and eventually sparked a youth protest movement that New Delhi tried to suppress with more deliberate internet outages. ®

item.title: Chinese web giant Tencent says new US GPU ban ‘sets everyone back in China’
item.description: The USA’s new ban on Chinese companies remotely accessing GPUs will have short-term impact, but ultimately see China accelerate its development of domestic alternatives, according to Martin Lau, the president of Chinese web giant Tencent. Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Lau said the new US regulation will have an “unfortunate” impact on Tencent’s business. “It does set everyone back. It sets everyone back in China,” Lau said. “So everyone is actually having less advanced compute to work with, no matter when you actually started leasing or building capacities outside of China.” He said the ban will impact Tencent’s ability to train models. “Our training efficiency with Hy4 is actually very high,” he said. “When we look at the next version, it would take probably longer time for us to come up with the next version in the short run.” “But over time, the domestic supply chain would actually come on board.” Lau also thinks the bans won’t hamper Tencent’s ability to run inferencing workloads, because made-in-China chips “should be able to cover it.” “And over the longer run, we believe all Chinese players would actually have to rely on domestic supply chains and domestic chips, which we see the industry is progressing very fast,” he added. “With the latest restriction, we expect it to actually speed up even further, because all the development effort would actually have to be focused on speeding up the domestic supply chain.” Tencent needs GPUs, and lots of them, because the 10 million users of its agentic assistant WorkBuddy are collectively consuming over 100 trillion tokens per day. Lau thinks WorkBuddy is on track to becoming a hit product, partly because many users are outside China. Lau said Tencent can serve WorkBuddy customers outside China because the service can operate with different models, and the company thinks it can find third parties to provide the necessary inferencing services without the new US bans creating a problem. But Lau said that GPU rentals and other cloud services, which are also growing strongly, may be impacted. “In terms of cloud, if it is non-GPU related, we can actually build capacities ourselves outside of China,” he said. “I think there is still a lot of such opportunities because our cloud service is actually very cost competitive. When it comes to GPU, then unfortunately, we cannot actually offer high-end GPU anymore. We may be able to work with some partners in different places.” Tencent doesn’t break out revenue for its cloud services, but said they rose by 35 percent year-on-year, well ahead of the company’s overall eight percent growth. Marketing services also grew strongly, by 19 percent, thanks in part to new AI-powered systems that improve ad targeting. The company’s WeChat and Weixin messaging platforms continued to grow, adding 35 million accounts to exiting the quarter with 1.44 billion monthly active users. item.title: Another critical PHP security release has dropped
item.description: Apologies in advance to all patch managers and security teams that thought they might get a break this week. The PHP Foundation has released several more patches, covering all supported versions, and including at least one rated “critical.” These fortunately were not leaked leaked like last month’s critical PHP2Shell flaws – but a Wednesday advisory warned, “The issues rated critical require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups,” urging PHP users to “prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available.” One of the vulnerabilities is another remote code execution (RCE) flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-115560. In October, the PHP Foundation told The Register that it had reserved this CVE identifier for another RCE bug, but added it would not get an emergency fix like the earlier two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities because the third one doesn't pose the same risk. CVE-2026-115560 “requires a very unlikely combination of configuration and specific PHP application code, which we do not expect to occur in practical use of PHP,” Elizabeth Barron, executive director of the PHP Foundation, told The Register at the time. “The issue can be mitigated with a configuration setting. So for the moment the PHP Security Team has only published an informational advisory on the PHP website, explaining exactly this situation.” The earlier informational advisory urged users to “set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector.” These unlikely RCE attacks require an application to set “ session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start() .” Additionally, the session upload progress feature must be enabled, which the PHP Foundation said is very unlikely in real-world applications. Overall, a large number of bugs were fixed and CVEs patched across five releases. Get more info on the PHP news page here. The November security releases follow a hectic October emergency PHP patch-a-thon , with security teams racing to apply fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called PHP2Shell, before attackers could abuse the memory-safety flaws in the open source programming language running on about 70 percent of websites. While it took miscreants longer to reverse engineer the PHP2Shell fixes than some researchers had anticipated – and the entire internet didn’t burn down in the meantime – the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) did add the two PHP vulns to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26. Suspected Chinese attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including Palo Alto Networks firewalls linked to US government-affiliated organizations, as early as October 23, according to Dream researchers. item.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
item.description: null Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect." In December 2025, observations from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope provided the final evidence that allowed researchers to fully reconstruct what happened before, during, and after the merger of a binary star system nicknamed Bao in the Andromeda galaxy. (Image credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia), Kishalay De (Columbia); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI); Acknowledgment: DSS, Robert Gendler) In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy . The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun . In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018. The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. As this companion spiraled toward the giant's core, it would generate friction, heat and light, explaining the increasing luminosity. Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. The researchers now propose that this explosion happened when a companion star about 70% the sun's mass rammed into the giant's heart. "I was absolutely flabbergasted when we saw this," Karambelkar said. In the new study, the scientists estimated that the eruption expelled an amount of material equal to about 0.1 to 0.2 times the mass of the sun . "Stars engulfing their companions have been theorized for many decades, and this event provides the first observations of this theoretical prediction," Karambelkar said. Although these findings suggest that two stars — a binary system nicknamed "Bao" — merged into one, "it is not the only possibility," Karambelkar said. item.title: Anthropic decides to go head-to-head with GTA VI release, schedules IPO for the same day
item.description: Well, it’s official: Anthropic will become the first publicly-traded frontier AI lab in history come the opening of markets on Thursday. The company kicked off its IPO roadshow last week, announcing plans to offer 825 million shares with an IPO price between $70 and $78 a share when sales begin Thursday. The company's most recent SEC filing cites that price range but allows for the possibility of a higher price, which should be determined Wednesday night. Late on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported that Anthropic would price at $83, citing people familiar. Whatever the case, Anthropic is likely to be valued at more than $1 trillion. Anthropic’s debutante ball has been on the horizon for a while, and documents leaked in late September made it all the more inevitable as the company’s finances revved up and it sought to capture the momentum of its best quarter to date before things start to tail off. The company revised its IPO documents on November 2, warning that the 12x growth it was touting was unlikely to continue in the long term due to compute infrastructure investments to the tune of nearly $900 billion it was on the hook for over the next few years. "In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our revenue was $33.2 billion, representing a year-over-year growth rate of 1,206%," the revised prospectus reads. "We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all." It’s possible, in other words, that Anthropic may never be a money maker despite the hype and its position as the first mover. The IPO prospectus is short on answers to critical questions and leaves a lot unanswered - like, for example, whether it’s going to actually be able to pay its bills. "Our ability to meet the substantial and growing financial obligations of these requirements to secure compute depends on our ability to generate significant revenue growth," the updated prospectus admits. Investors don’t seem to care right now, though. Anthropic already has compute commitments amounting to roughly $70.7 billion in the next 12 months. That’s just shy of its $81 billion run-rate as of October 31. Expect more hot air to be injected tomorrow, adding additional surface tension and the possibility of even more losses if, and when, this monster pops. ®

item.title: AI found more critical bugs in another widely used technology running 225M websites
item.description: Hot on the heels of serious vulnerabilities in seemingly every other widely used software powering the entire internet, F5 today released emergency patches for 10 bugs in open source NGINX. These include critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers hijack NGINX servers with HTTP/2 enabled, as well as the millions of websites running NGINX, to steal sensitive data and disrupt services. “At this time, we have found no evidence of active exploitation of any of these vulnerabilities in the wild,” and F5 spokesperson told The Register . “We continue to monitor closely and will share updates via myF5 as we learn more.” As with all of the other recently disclosed vulnerabilities in foundational technologies like PHP, Apache, and Java, these critical NGINX bugs were uncovered by researchers using AI. One of them has been hiding in the code for at least 10 years. Tomer Schwartz, Wiz’s chief technology officer of exposure management and AppSec, helped find the bug, along with researchers from Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint working independently. Schwartz told The Register that this wave of AI-discovered flaws “point to a new reality.” “We need to treat every internet-connected system as potentially vulnerable,” Schwartz said. “AI has changed not only which vulnerabilities can be found, but how quickly longstanding risks can become real threats.” NGINX is the world’s most widely used open source web server, handling HTTPS requests and routing incoming traffic to the right application or API. It powers about a third of all websites (around 225 million ), and F5 maintains the open source version. On Wednesday, F5 published an out-of-band security notification that addressed 10 CVEs in open source NGINIX. If you run NGINX, update to 1.31.9 as soon as possible. CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 Two of the vulns are especially serious as they allow a remote attacker to execute code on the NGINX server without authentication. These two, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 , both received a critical, 9.2 CVSS rating, and CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. All of the security shops listed earlier independently found at least one of these two CVEs - most, if not all, with an AI assist - and reported them to F5. “Both vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues in how NGINX handles HTTP/2 traffic,” Schwartz and fellow Wiz kid Nir Ohfeld said in a Wednesday blog about the two bugs. “In CVE-2026-123633, a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, creating a use-after-free. In CVE-2026-123007, incorrect flow-control accounting leads to an invalid memory copy.” Rapid7’s team also published a proof-of-concep t to demonstrate leveraging CVE-2026-123007 for unauthenticated remote code execution against a vulnerable linux/amd64 Docker image running nginx version 1.31.8. Xint found three other NGINX flaws, plus a sepa

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
item.description: null On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface , and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place. An Atlas V rocket launches NASA's Mars MAVEN orbiter into space from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Base on Nov. 18, 2013. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) Why it mattered NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind , as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time. After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014 . The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind. An artist's view of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft at Mars on a mission to study its upper atmosphere. (Image credit: NASA) "The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come." MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study. NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent , with NASA losing communication with the orbiter. An investigation later found that the probe sent its final signal on Dec. 6, 2025 as it was heading behind Mars (as seen from Earth). item.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
item.description: null More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged. In the Grand Canyon, rock layers separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, revealing a vast gap in Earth's geological record. (Image credit: Marcia Straub via Getty Images) One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity. It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years. "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement . "The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance." The Great Unconformity imaged here shows 550 million year old Tapeats Sandstone resting on 1.7 billion year old Vishnu Schist, in Blacktail Canyon along the Colorado River in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. (Image credit: William Dummitt via Getty Images) What erased the geological record? In a new study published in the journal Nature, Dhungana and study co-author Nicolas Flament investigated whether activity far below Earth's surface was to blame. Using computer models, they explored how the slow circulation of hot rock within Earth's mantle may have affected the continents over hundreds of millions of years. The results suggest that three major ancient continental regions (Laurentia (modern North America), Baltica (northern Europe) and North China were gradually pushed up during the Neoproterozoic Era, approximately one billion to 540 million years ago. This would have left vast areas of land exposed to weathering and erosion for long periods, allowing water, wind and other processes to wear away rock that had formed much earlier. But removing the rock is only part of the puzzle. They also needed to explain why the gaps

item.title: Tunji Olowolafe Wants Ikogosi to Be Nigeria’s Next Destination for Weddings, Retreats and Landmark Celebrations
item.description: Growing up, Tunji Olowolafe ’s parents brought the family to Are-Ekiti every Christmas, and a trip to Ikogosi was compulsory. Decades later, he returned to the warm springs town with family, friends and business partners, “not to take away, but to help build something enduring in Ekiti.” Speaking as Chairman and Chief Launcher of Ikogosi Day 2026, Thanksgiving and Launch of the Oba’s Palace Project, on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the Chancellor of Ekiti State University set out a vision for Ikogosi built on intentional tourism, enterprise and heritage. Dr. Olowolafe said Ikogosi’s task now is to give visitors compelling reasons to come, stay longer and spend across local businesses. He pointed to the recent Ikogosi 17.5km Race, which drew runners from across Nigeria alongside athletes from Ghana, Kenya and Ethiopia, as an example of what happens when private initiative meets local hospitality. He urged the same thinking for lifestyle and executive tourism, with the ambition of making Ikogosi a premier international destination for weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate retreats and landmark gatherings. “Our natural landscape will draw people in. But only the quality of the experience we deliver, through warmth of welcome, impeccable service and attention to detail, will bring them back,” he said. To build that service culture, he called for a deeper, structured partnership between the Ikogosi Resort and the Hospitality Management Technology Department of the Federal Polytechnic, Ado-Ekiti, which has already produced two sets of National Diploma graduates. The goal is for students to train alongside seasoned professionals while serving real guests. He also proposed alliances with leading international hospitality institutes to benchmark local teaching and service, noting that world-class hospitality must become Ekiti’s signature. He argued that the same commercial discipline must apply to the resources beneath the ground. “It is not enough to say we have clay or kaolin. We must ask: What are their exact industrial specifications? What can we competitively manufacture? And who is ready to buy?” he said. He tasked the Department of Geology at Ekiti State University, headed by Professor Yinka Aturamu , with establishing precise data on local deposits and mapping out what it would take to turn them into viable commercial enterprises. For him, the measure of success is what it changes for young people in the community. “For a young person growing up in Ikogosi, the result must be tangible: a marketable skill, a steady job, a supply contract or a thriving enterprise,” he said. He cited Rasheed Sarumi’s Saroafrica Group as proof of what is possible. The group acquired Gossy Warm Springs in 2018 and restored the plant to full production in 2019. Together with its partners, Saroafrica is now investing US$25 million in a manufacturing facility in Ikogosi, which will run on its own 2MW gas-fired power plant. item.title: Miss Universe 2026: Meet the 17 African Queens Representing the Continent
item.description: From left: Miss Universe Democratic Republic of the Congo 2026 Jessi Kalambayi, Miss Universe Namibia 2026 Charene Labuschagne, and Miss Universe Botswana 2026 Dabilo Moses ahead of the 75th Miss Universe finale in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Miss Universe stage is getting a beautiful dose of African representation this year, with 17 contestants from across the continent making their way to Puerto Rico for the pageant’s 75th edition. And there are plenty of stories to discover among them, from Uganda ’s historic debut to Nigeria ’s Danielle Adewusi , whose journey to the competition comes with a lovely family connection. Taking place in San Juan, Puerto Rico, the Diamond Anniversary edition will bring together 116 contestants from around the world, all hoping to claim the newly unveiled 75th-anniversary crown, The Radiance of an Eternal Legacy. The grand finale is scheduled for Tuesday, 24 November 2026, at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum. This year’s show will be hosted by R’Bonney Gabriel , Mario Lopez , Zuri Hall and Dayanara Torres . At the end of the night, reigning Miss Universe 2025 Fátima Bosch of Mexico will pass on her crown to a new winner. Bosch took the title in Thailand last November, ahead of contestants from Thailand, Venezuela, the Philippines and Côte d’Ivoire. item.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
item.description: null United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own issues at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28 , and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.) ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's update. Vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit. In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance. Vulcan Centaur rises into the sky on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure. Vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

item.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. It provided an intentional platform for candid conversations, practical insights and strategic alliances on what it takes for women to advance, lead and thrive in today’s evolving corporate landscape. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. According to her, competence is merely the baseline; it is not enough if you are unwilling to communicate your value, own your voice and position yourself for higher-stakes opportunities. This philosophy also came through in her cover interview with THISDAY Glitterati ahead of the summit, where she offered a compelling perspective on the distinction between holding a powerful position and exercising genuine influence. “A powerful position gives you formal authority. Influence determines how deeply your leadership shapes people’s thinking, decisions and actions. A title may secure your place in a meeting, but credibility makes people listen,” she explained. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? What result did you produce? item.title: 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket?
item.description: null The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket. NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet . But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one. "It is clear that SkyFall was approved for programmatic or political reasons," said Scott Hubbard, former director of NASA's Ames Research Center and the first Mars Program Director (aka the " Mars Czar ") at NASA Headquarters, told Space.com. "The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'" Shotgun marriage? Hubbard is a retired adjunct professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University. He is a major voice in shaping Red Planet exploration goals, drawing upon his expertise as NASA's former foremost Mars authority. His understanding is that the basic concept had been developed as a follow on to Ingenuity, an attempt to move beyond a technology demo and into a science platform. Hubbard said that combining these two observations, the outcome presents "an unusual set of management issues." Since the SkyFall mission concept first appeared, he said, the usual sequence for a science mission is reversed. "The science community is having to scramble to back into a set of requirements and objectives that match the SkyFall capabilities. Fortunately the community is very creative," said Hubbard, "and the basic Planetary Decadal objectives are very broad." Decadal surveys reflect a broad consensus within the scientific community and provide detailed insights into the strategic priorities and mission directives set for the next decade across key scientific domains, including planetary exploration. Lemonade squeeze However, Hubbard said he has heard griping about the "fait accompli" process, "but the planetary community will make lemonade." It should be noted however, Hubbard continued, that this process is not how you would design a strategic set of missions as precursors for human exploration. "SR-1 Freedom is a technology demo that may or may not be ready for the Mars launch window in 2028. It is clear that the Mars Program has a standard launch concept in their back pocket," said Hubbard. "Nuclear Electric Propulsion [NEP] is of little value in traveling to Mars, not shaving any time off the transit. The real value of NEP is for risk reduction, use at the moon, ou

The exceptional sci-fi movie, based on Andy Weir's book, stars Ryan Gosling as Ryland Grace, a middle-school science teacher who becomes key to saving the world. Together with Rocky, an alien he meets along the way, Grace must solve the riddle of the mysterious substance that's causing the sun (and Rocky's star) to die out. Amazon MGM has revealed the return to theaters with a video showcasing the many accolades that the film received. (Image credit: MGM) "Project Hail Mary" was a massive success for Amazon MGM, grossing over $600 million worldwide when it first dropped in theaters back in March 2026. It was also a huge hit with critics, scoring an average of 95% on Rotten Tomatoes , and more importantly, getting two big thumbs up in our review ! Dec. 11 is a smart choice by MGM too, as it puts the sci-fi spectacle back in front of audiences a week ahead of Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3. That's not a battle you want to get in the middle of. If you missed "Project Hail Mary" in theaters the first time, I'd definitely recommend you try to catch one of these screenings. If you're not feeling up to a trip to the theaters, you can also catch "Project Hail Mary" from the comfort of your own home, as it's also streaming on Amazon Prime Video. item.title: Supernova explodes before astronomers' eyes | Space photo of the day for Nov. 18, 2026
item.description: null Before-and-after photos showing the appearance of a new supernova designated SN 2026ahvu. (Image credit: Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Acknowledgment: PIs: G. Narayan & T. Murphey (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign) Image processing: M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)) A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth. What is it? Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf . During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion. Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter. This indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place. Why is it incredible? Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres. ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system. But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova. Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.

item.title: The Lego Star Trek bridge diorama set should be your gateway to finally watching the Original Series
item.description: null It's not quite a five-year mission, but as Star Trek celebrated its 60th anniversary in September of this year (we may have mentioned it once or twice), I decided it was high time I finally watched the original Star Trek . Before this year, I hadn't seen a single episode of "Star Trek: The Original Series", as it's now known. I'm a millennial; I grew up on "The Next Generation", "Deep Space Nine" and "Voyager". By comparison, the old series (TOS) always looked so… old and naff whenever I saw clips of it. But now I have seen the original series. Over the course of 2026, I've ploughed through all 79 episodes, spread across three seasons. And you know what? It's pretty damn good. Even with the shiny 2006 remasters, you'll have to prepare yourself for some bad special effects work, but the scripts are interesting, the sci-fi concepts are out there, and the acting — especially from Shatner and Nimoy — is top-notch. And just as I finally discovered a love for this classic sci-fi series, what should drop into my lap? Why it's the new Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge diorama set from Lego. Now I have more on my wishlist to add to the Best lego space sets. Boldly building where no one has built before Building the Lego Star Trek: Bridge diorama. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Let's start with the Band-Aid rip: this set is $200. I know; it stings, especially when Star Trek promised us a future where money doesn't exist. But at 1701 pieces (nice, I see what you did there), it's much better value from a bricks-per-dollar perspective than the X-Files set we checked out recently. Still, that's no small investment for a toy, even if it will make a lovely display piece when it's built. As the name suggests, you get a full Lego-ified recreation of the bridge of the USS Enterprise (NCC-1701, no A, B, C, or D). This includes Captain Kirk's chair, the helm positions ahead of him (manned by Chekov and Sulu), and all of the surrounding computer displays where you usually find Spock, Uhura and Scotty. There's even a viewscreen that can sit in front of the crew, displaying an adorable Klingon commander facing off against Kirk. The minifigure bridge crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise (L-R): Nurse Chapel, Chekov, Scotty, Spock, Kirk, McCoy, Uhura and Sulu. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Star Trek: U.S.S. item.title: India's SatLeo Labs wants to build a 'thermometer for Earth' in space
item.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

AHMEDABAD, India — As climate disasters grow more frequent and severe, a young Indian space-tech startup is betting it can help the world act sooner by reading Earth's temperature from orbit in near-real time. SatLeo Labs, based here in western India, is building what it calls a " thermometer for Earth " in space. It plans to achieve its roadmap to deliver frequent, near-real-time thermal data through Pyro, a planned constellation of 15 microsatellites that will circle the planet in low Earth orbit by early 2030, if all goes to plan. Equipped with thermal sensors and onboard artificial intelligence , the satellites will measure the heat radiating from Earth's surface at a resolution finer than 10 meters (33 feet), which is sharp enough to map heat variations down to street level, the company says. "It's going to be that precise," SatLeo Labs co-founder Urmil Bakhai told Space.com in a recent interview. That level of detail, he said, helps distinguish temperatures across a single city and pinpoint urban hot spots, allowing governments and policymakers to plan targeted interventions and more heat-resilient city designs. The company is also targeting agriculture, and for good reason: Research suggests that thermal data can directly reveal water stress on crops days before leaves wilt, discolor or show other visible damage, unlike visible-light satellite imagery. Other uses the company is eyeing include spotting forest fires early, tracking industrial emissions and, on the defense side, detecting sudden temperature spikes from missile launches . Down the road, the team also envisions hyper-local uses. Near the top of its list are live heat maps built into navigation apps that could help gig-economy workers in India. These folks, who often ride motorcycles, could use the data to pick cooler routes during heat waves, said Bakhai. "We are in space, but we're solving problems on Earth ," said Shravan Bhati, SatLeo's co-founder and CEO. First, however, the company has to prove that its homegrown hardware works in space. On Oct. 1, SatLeo launched its first technology demonstrator, TAPAS-1, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission. Short for "Thermal Access Platform for Analytics & Solutions," TAPAS-1 is India's first commercial thermal payload in orbit and the first of SatLeo's three planned test payloads meant to validate its technology. Once complete, the 15-satellite Pyro fleet will scan all of the world's land surface at least twice a day, Bakhai said. Successful deployment of that fleet would make SatLeo one of just a few private thermal-imaging operators across the world, such as SatVu in the U.K. and OroraTech in Germany. The
